a2-unit-37.37.1 The Feel Good podcast:
Host: Hi everyone! Thanks for joining us on Feel Good. We usually talk about food and cooking, but today we're going to discuss well-being. My guest is Priya. She's a medical student here in Chicago, and she also teaches yoga at her local community center. Priya, I want to start by asking you to define well-being.
Priya: Sure. We hear a lot about well-being these days, and it simply means feeling healthy and happy. The two things go together. You can't really be healthy if you're not happy. And to be healthy, we need to move.
Host: How much exercise do we really need?
Priya: According to the CDC, adults need at least a hundred and fifty minutes of moderate activity a week. That's about thirty minutes a day, five days a week. Fast walking is fine!
Host: OK. But I think many of us feel that exercise is something we have to do, even if it's boring.
Priya: That's so true. What I say is this. If you dislike exercising, you should consider changing activities.
Host: Well, that's me! I always avoid going to the gym. I try to go once a week, but really, I only go once a month.
Priya: It sounds like you need a change! A lot of people enjoy exercising if they can be outside. Running is an activity you can do in your local park. Or you might think about cycling.
Host: I used to ride my bike to work. I miss cycling! And running sounds OK when the weather's nice. But what about if it's raining? Or when it's dark and cold in the winter?
Priya: In bad weather, you can keep cycling. Just go to a spin class! Or you can try a dance class. Dancing is a really fun workout.
Host: And what type of exercise do you do?
Priya: For me, yoga is the best way to keep fit and stay happy. I also go running along the lake once a week, whatever the weather. Believe it or not, I actually look forward to running in the snow!
Host: I guess you've found the right routine. Thanks for your advice!
Priya: It's a pleasure.
